name: Data, information and answers as a service (IoT analytics)
summary: The provider earns money from data produced by connected devices at three levels of processing: raw data (DaaS), derived information (IaaS) or ready answers and recommendations (AaaS). One consultancy article names Schneider Electric's EcoStruxure Asset Advisor as an AaaS example. The same article warns that few companies build a sustainable model on data.
how_it_makes_money: Per the source: DaaS is priced per data unit (most common), by subscription or flat rate. IaaS is priced per call or order, or with a free tier tied to registered data. AaaS is priced per answer or by subscription for frequent use, plus consulting or implementation fees. No energy-specific prices were found.

hardware: Connected devices or sensors that produce the data
sites_assets: Customer assets that are instrumented (buildings, plants, equipment)
partners: Implementation partners (the source advises engaging the right ones early)
channel: Close customer contact (the source names it as a condition for answers-as-a-service)
data: Incentives for customers to keep sharing when the initial data is limited

stakeholder_value.customer: Data, information or recommendations they do not produce themselves
stakeholder_value.provider: Recurring or usage-based revenue from data it already has access to

what_must_be_true: Data quality is high and measured regularly
The customer's problem is confirmed in interviews and an early proof of concept
The offer fits into the customer's own process
Willingness to pay is tested early, for example through demo or beta use or letters of intent
For DaaS: a dominant role in the industry and high data volume
For AaaS: close customer contact and deep knowledge of the customers

risks_failure_causes.text: Companies often overestimate the value of their data and their ability to earn revenue from it; few reach a sustainable model (observation by a consultancy, no study cited)
Bad data quality and blind trust in data without context. The source's example is a non-energy company that found 70 percent of its logistics data was incorrect
Shortage of data talent and underestimated skill requirements
With limited initial data, customers must be given reasons to keep sharing
The solution does not fit the customer's process, or customer needs were never validated

cases.note: Named in the source as an example of answers-as-a-service. The source gives no revenue, pricing or results.

Digital building offerings: energy consumption monitoring, sustainability reporting, space utilisation, predictive maintenance. Open questions were which solutions clients need, willingness to pay and whether facility managers differ by region. A workable pricing model was reached but not disclosed. The page's results section describes an ag-tech pilot, so treat this case as thin.
